points.text: SOVERN — production stack for agent pipelines
Rakes that cost me days of debugging (save these, no need to step on them yourself):
Rake 1: Double cloudflared = 502 flapping I ran cloudflared both via systemd on the host and as a Docker container — with the same tunnel token.
Rake 2: Public IP as tunnel origin I routed n8n.example.com → :5678.
Rake 3: Langfuse v3 without ClickHouse Langfuse v3 requires ClickHouse + Redis (~2GB extra RAM).
Rake 4: n8n API doesn't work from outside curl https://n8n.example.com/api/v1 from the outside returns 200, but Python urllib gets 403 (apparently, CF challenge headers).
Scripts that hit the n8n API have to run on the server itself, against http://localhost:5678/api/v1.
Two weeks later you can drop in and see what exactly AI replied for a specific email at 03:47 in the morning.

points: SOVERN is a production stack for agent pipelines that includes debugging lessons to help you avoid mistakes.
Running cloudflared twice with the same token or routing a public IP as a tunnel origin causes errors like 502 flapping.
Langfuse v3 requires ClickHouse and Redis, and scripts for the n8n API must run on the server itself to avoid 403 errors.
You can use a 5-fallback LLM routing pattern and Langfuse to see exactly what the AI replied at 03:47 in the morning.
